questions: Should the median be computed on the original order of elements, or should the list be sorted first?
For an even-length list, should the median be the average of the two middle values (as a float) or one of them (e.g., lower)?
If the list contains non-numeric elements (e.g., strings), should the function handle them, raise an error, or assume numeric?
Should the median be returned as the same type as the elements (e.g., int for ints) or always as a float when averaging?
Is the list guaranteed to be non-empty, or should the function handle empty lists?
Should the function treat duplicate values in the list specially, or just include them normally?
Does 'middle value' refer to the median after sorting, or the element at the middle index of the original list?
If the list is large, are there performance constraints (e.g., O(n log n) sorting allowed)?
